videos.t: I Built a Foldable CyberDeck (Internal Breadboards)
videos.desc:
I'm planning to make some robotics-related videos in the future. Apart from animations, these involve a lot of filming in real life, so I made this short video about my CyberDeck to practice filming, recording, and editing.

Check out the CyberDeck subreddit, I got a lot of inspiration from other people's builds: https://www.reddit.com/r/cyberDeck/

If you want to replicate my build, I uploaded the files here: https://www.printables.com/model/1583012-handheld-foldable-cyberdeck-cyberplug-30

videos.t: Recognizing Numbers With a Glass of Water
videos.desc: This is my first edited shorts test. It explores the number detector idea from my long-form video where I used the principle of water accumulation for feature extraction.

videos.t: Neat Math Trick to Detect Circles (Circle Hough Transform)
videos.desc:
I decided to make a little short video to celebrate Pi Day. In the video I visually explain, in a simplified way, how the Circle Hough Transform works. Happy Pi Day!

Music: Meydän - Pure Water (CC BY 4.0)
Changes made: The track is slowed down.
Link: https://freemusicarchive.org/music/Meydan/Interplanetary_Forest/Meydn_-_Interplanetary_Forest_-_02_Pure_Water

Inspired by the Artemis II mission, I started building a procedural planet renderer using ray marching and ray tracing. After finishing it, I had a crazy idea to run the algorithm (on ESP32) using power from a hot air/Stirling engine. I set the renderer's output as my profile picture, so I guess I can say my profile picture was made by a hot air engine.

Music Used:
Continental Drift by Jay Taylor
Time Zones by Gavin Luke

videos.t: This Computer Works as Long as I Have Fire
videos.desc:
I recently got into building cyberdecks and thought, why not make a DIY computer inspired by steampunk instead of cyberpunk?

Here's the result: an ESP32-based contraption powered entirely by a Stirling engine.
